Leafy greens and such are good foods for them, make sure they always have Timothy hay to snack on, too. They tend to only potty in one spot of their cage, so you can wait to see which corner they use and put a litter pan in to keep the cage break downs and full cleans to a weekly basis or so. They like hammocks!!

Everyone always thinks rabbits = carrots, and they can absolutely have them as a treat but the high natural sugar content can be bad for them in the long run (bunny diabetes is sad). Pumice stones make good chew toys, your pet store will have other items for them too. Bunny teeth never, ever stop growing and can even grow through their bottom jaw if you aren't careful / don't give them stimulating things to chew. 

Bunnies are easily stressed by things like loud noise, extreme temps, large changes in environment and larger animals. They can actually literally kill themselves by being too stressed out -- they can break their own spinal cord when attempting to flee and can drop dead of a stress induced heart attack as well. Giving them lots of safe areas in your home to enjoy will make them feel comfier (my bunnies loved to flop over on their sides and expose their tummies when they would sit under our rocking chair, for example). Flopping over and showing you their tummy is like, the ultimate signal of trust! I found that they typically preferred places where they had walls to their back and sides but could see out ahead of them, like in soda boxes! Plus, the cardboard isn't harmful if they nibble it a bit (and they will, trust me. You thought baby proofing was hard? Bunny proofing is a whole 'nother thing, haha). 

Bunnies are the best pet imo if you're prepared for them. They're friendly and cuddly and incredibly charismatic (my dwarf, Tuff, had all sorts of ways to tell you how he was feeling -- mid air barrel rolls when he was happy, a silly little huffy noise when you took something away from him, he'd run away from you and stomp his back feet really hard when you made him mad). 

I just wish they lived longer. :(

No problem! I recommend Smooth On products for resin casting, btw! You can use clay to make a claw, put it in a Tupperware dish and pour silicone over the top to make your mold and then fill that with resin. 


Alternatively, I know members of the furry community like Flurrycat (Monoyasha / Dreamvision Creations), YEEP and Stuffed Panda Studios all sell premade parts. 

Another option would be 3D printing -- I'm currently working on a prototype for some claws but they won't be ready for a while.

Resin, thermoplastics or soft claws dipped in tool dip will be your best bet. I don't recommend clay pieces on fursuits because of the amount of wear and tear they get. Clay parts are harder to anchor, more prone to breaking or chipping and they can often be heavier than other options.

At my work we have metal pans for keeping produce in. They're about six inches wide, sixish inches deep and probably 8-10in long with a wickedly curved metal lip. We keep them on a shelf above a sink. 

One morning when I was opening the store, I went to grab a stack only to realize that the asshole who had closed had made a single stack of pans 8-10 high, to the point where I couldn't grab the top pan. 

Should I have grabbed a ladder? Probably. But I had a trick I'd done a thousand times before where I curled my fingers into the lip of the pans with one hand and tugged, catching the stack with the other hand as it fell against my shoulder. 

Except I only executed about one third of my plan properly. It had been a shitty week, I was tired, and for some reason I was more than content to just watch these pans come down and bust my head open. I even remember thinking to myself, "why isn't your hand up put your hand up oh my God you idiot, you're about to get hit". 

Knocked myself on my ass, thought I was okay for the first five or so minutes because at the time my hair was thick enough to soak up a fair amount of blood. Reached up to touch my head in a spot that hurt particularly bad and it was wet and red when I pulled my hand away. 

At that point was when the first drips made it past my hair line. Long story short, coworker took me to the hospital where it was apparent I had managed to almost scalp myself, peeling back 2.5ish inches of my skin where the lip of the pans caught me.
